title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
Symptom: Clicking Generate produces no output, a timeout error, or a generic “AI generation failed” message.
Causes and fixes: - The AI service can take 15–30 seconds for longer workflows (Lesson Drafter in particular). Wait at least 30 seconds before concluding it has failed. - Check your AI credit balance in Settings. If you have 0 credits, generation will be blocked immediately. - If generation consistently fails, the AI service may be temporarily unavailable. Try again in a few minutes. - Very long file content (over 50,000 characters) will be rejected. Split large files into multiple lessons.




Symptom: Creating a course returns a duplicate title error.
Fix: Course slugs must be unique per account. Choose a different title, or append a year or version number (e.g. “Introduction to Python 2026”).




Symptom: Clicking “Commit to GitHub” shows an error.
Causes and fixes: - Your GitHub connection may have expired. Go to Settings, disconnect, and reconnect. - The repository may have been deleted manually on GitHub. CourseFoundry will attempt to recreate it on the next commit. - GitHub’s API may be temporarily unavailable. Check githubstatus.com and retry. - If you recently revoked CourseFoundry’s GitHub access from your GitHub account settings, reconnect from Settings.




Symptom: You published a course but it doesn’t appear in the catalog.
Causes and fixes: - Allow up to 30 seconds after publishing for the catalog to update. Refresh the page. - Confirm the course is showing as Published (green badge) on your dashboard. If it shows Draft, the publish action may not have saved — click the globe icon again. - If the course appears on your dashboard as Published but is missing from the catalog, try unpublishing and republishing.




Symptom: The lesson list on the public course page doesn’t match what you expect.
Fix: The sidebar order on the rendered site is determined by _quarto.yml. CourseFoundry regenerates this file automatically when you show or hide folders, but if you have manually edited _quarto.yml the auto-regeneration will overwrite your changes the next time you toggle visibility. To fine-tune ordering, open _quarto.yml in the editor — just be aware that a visibility toggle will regenerate it. File and folder names with a numeric prefix (e.g. 01-, 02-) sort alphabetically and therefore control the order reliably.




Credits reset automatically on the 1st of each month. You cannot manually reset them. If you need more credits before the reset, upgrade your plan or wait for the monthly reset.




Yes. Open your course in the editor, click the LMS Export tab in the right panel, then click Download SCORM Package. The package can be uploaded to any SCORM-compliant LMS (Moodle, Blackboard, Brightspace, etc.).

Note: All course content must be visible (not hidden) before downloading a SCORM package. If any folders are hidden via the Eye toggle, an amber warning appears and the download button is replaced with a prompt to unhide all content first.

PDF export is planned for a future release. Your source files are standard Quarto Markdown — if you have GitHub integration enabled, you can clone your repository and run quarto render locally to produce any output format Quarto supports.




Use the Eye toggle in the file tree. Hover over a week or module folder and click the Eye icon to hide it. Hidden folders are excluded from the published sidebar — students cannot navigate to them even if they know the URL.
Each week before you want content to go live: 1. Hover the folder in the file tree and click the EyeOff icon to reveal it 2. The sidebar is regenerated automatically 3. Commit and push — GitHub Actions re-renders the site and the new week appears for students




Yes. All courses are private by default (Draft status). Only you can see your draft courses — not other CourseFoundry users, not the public. Your content is only made public if you explicitly click the Publish button.
Once published, the course is publicly accessible without login. Unpublishing immediately reverts the course to private.




Team collaboration is planned for the Enterprise plan (Phase 17). Currently, each course belongs to one account. As a workaround, you can share a GitHub repository with a collaborator who can make changes outside CourseFoundry and you can sync them via a commit.




Account deletion is currently handled by contacting support. Send a request to support@coursefoundry.com and your account, courses, and data will be deleted within 30 days in accordance with our Privacy Policy.





This document — covers all current features
Support email: support@coursefoundry.com
Feature requests and bug reports: github.com/johnfjennings/coursefoundry/issues (public issue tracker, coming soon)


CourseFoundry is actively developed. Features marked “coming soon” or “planned” are subject to change. This document is updated with each major release.

AI Credits A consumable resource that is deducted each time you run an AI Forge workflow or send a chat message. Credits reset monthly. Each plan includes a different monthly allowance.
Assessment A file (typically assessment.qmd) containing questions, exercises, or activities used to test learner understanding. Generated by the Assessment Builder workflow.
Chapter A file listed in _quarto.yml. Chapters define the order of lessons in the published course.
Course A container for all your course content — files, settings, metadata, and publishing status.
Course Files The individual .qmd, .yml, and other files that make up the course content, stored in CourseFoundry’s database.
Draft The default status of a course. Draft courses are private — only the author can see them. A draft course can be edited freely without affecting any public-facing content.
Forge / AI Forge The AI copilot built into the editor. Includes 7 workflows (Outline, Lesson, Slides, Assessment, Review, Import, Chat) powered by Claude (Anthropic).
Module A folder within the course file structure that groups related lessons. Modules use the naming convention 01-module-name/.
Published A course status that makes the course publicly accessible at coursefoundry.com/learn/[username]/[slug]. Anyone can read a published course without an account.
Quarto An open-source technical publishing system built on Pandoc. CourseFoundry uses Quarto Markdown (.qmd) as its native content format. You do not need to install Quarto to use CourseFoundry.
Reveal.js An open-source presentation framework. The Slide Generator workflow produces Quarto files that can be rendered as Reveal.js presentations (e.g. via quarto render).
Slug The URL-safe version of a course title used in the course’s public URL. Generated automatically at course creation. Cannot be changed. The full public URL is /learn/[username]/[slug] — the slug alone is unique per user, not globally.
Snapshot A full copy of a course’s files committed to GitHub at a point in time, created by the GitHub integration’s Commit function.
Placeholder Image A generated SVG image used as a stand-in while a course is being built. Created from the Media panel by entering a description and dimensions. Stored in Supabase Storage and inserted into the active file as a standard Markdown image link. Replace placeholders with final images later without breaking the document structure.
Staged Publishing A workflow for releasing course content incrementally. Folders (weeks, modules) can be hidden from the published site using the Eye toggle in the file tree. Hidden folders are excluded from _quarto.yml automatically — so students only see the content you have chosen to reveal. Useful for semester courses where each week’s material is unlocked on a schedule.
_quarto.yml The course’s configuration file. Defines the sidebar navigation for the published website — which folders and files appear, and in what order. CourseFoundry manages this file automatically: it is regenerated whenever you show or hide a folder using the Eye toggle. You do not normally need to edit it by hand, but you can open it in the editor to inspect or fine-tune the sidebar structure.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
This section describes what the people you share your course with will see — no account required for learners.


The public catalog at coursefoundry.com/learn lists all published courses from all authors. Each course card shows: - Course title - Author - Description - Template type
Learners can browse and click any course to view it.

Note: There is currently no filtering or search on the catalog. Filtering and categorisation are planned for a future release.




A curated Community section at coursefoundry.com/learn/community lists courses that have been submitted for community review and approved. Authors can submit their published course for community listing from within the editor. Approved courses have the In Community badge on the dashboard.



Course landing page — Lists all lessons in order. Click any lesson to open it.
Lesson viewer — Shows the lesson content with: - Lesson title as heading - Full Markdown content rendered to HTML - Quarto callout blocks rendered with appropriate styling (tip, note, warning, important) - Code blocks with syntax highlighting - Previous and Next buttons for sequential navigation - Breadcrumb trail at the top showing: course name → module → lesson



Once published, share your course by copying the URL from the address bar when viewing the lesson viewer, or by sharing the course landing page URL directly:
https://coursefoundry.com/learn/[your-username]/[course-slug]
This URL works for anyone, anywhere — no account or login required.
Your username appears in Settings → Public Profile. The URL is unique to you — two authors can create courses with the same title without their URLs colliding.

text:
Access settings at /settings via the link in the navigation.


The Public Profile card shows your username and lets you change it.
Your username is the first segment in all your published course URLs:
https://coursefoundry.com/learn/[username]/[course-slug]
Your username is auto-generated from your email address when you sign up. You can change it here at any time.
Username rules: - 3–30 characters - Lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only - Must start and end with a letter or number

Warning: Changing your username updates all your course URLs immediately. Any previously shared links will stop working. Let your learners know if you change it.




The GitHub section shows whether your GitHub account is connected. From here you can: - Connect GitHub — start the OAuth flow - Disconnect — remove the connection (does not affect your GitHub repos)
See GitHub Integration for full details.



The billing section shows: - Your current plan and its features - AI credits used this month vs. your limit (progress bar) - Trial expiry date (Starter plan) - Buttons to upgrade or manage your subscription

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
All your courses appear on the dashboard as cards. They are sorted by most recently edited. Courses are private by default (Draft status) until you publish them.



Click the Copy icon on a course card to duplicate it. The duplicate is created with: - A new title: “[Original Title] (Copy)” - All original files copied - Status set to Draft - A new unique slug
Duplication is useful for creating course variants, seasonal updates, or using an existing course as a starting template.



Click the Trash icon on a course card. A confirmation modal appears explaining exactly what will happen before anything is deleted.
Permanently deleted: - The course record and all metadata - All course files and their content
Not affected: - Your GitHub repository (if linked) — the repo remains in your GitHub account; only the link between CourseFoundry and the repo is removed - AI credits already used — these are not refunded
Click Delete Course in the modal to confirm. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.



The slug is generated from the course title when the course is created. For example, a title of “Introduction to Smart Manufacturing” becomes the slug introduction-to-smart-manufacturing.
The published URL for a course is: coursefoundry.com/learn/[slug]
Slugs cannot be changed after course creation. If you need a different URL, create a new course with the desired title and migrate your content.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
CourseFoundry autosaves your work continuously to its own database. GitHub integration adds an additional layer: versioned snapshots. Every time you commit, a complete copy of your course files is pushed to a private GitHub repository.
This gives you: - Version history — go back to any previous state - Disaster recovery — restore your course if you accidentally delete content - Portability — your content lives in a standard Git repo you own - GitHub Pages publishing — automatically render and publish your course as a website (see below) - Collaboration potential — others can clone, fork, or contribute via GitHub




Go to Settings (link in the sidebar or top nav)
Scroll to the GitHub section
Click Connect GitHub
You’ll be redirected to GitHub to authorise CourseFoundry
After authorising, you’re returned to Settings with your GitHub username shown

You only need to connect once. The connection persists across sessions.




Open a course in the editor
Click the Git tab in the right panel
Write a commit message describing what you changed (e.g. “Add module 2 lessons” or “Fix assessment answers”)
Click Commit to GitHub

On the first commit for a course, CourseFoundry automatically creates a private GitHub repository named coursefoundry-[course-slug] in your GitHub account. Subsequent commits push to the same repository.
A success message shows the commit SHA and a link to view it on GitHub.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
When your course is ready for learners, publish it from the editor.
Click the globe icon in the editor toolbar. The icon changes to a filled globe and the status badge on your dashboard card changes from Draft to Published.
Published courses: - Appear on the public catalog at coursefoundry.com/learn - Are accessible at coursefoundry.com/learn/[your-course-slug] - Can be read by anyone — no account required



The public learn experience has two views:
Course landing page (/learn/[slug]) - Course title and description - Target audience and estimated duration (if set) - Full lesson list in the order defined by _quarto.yml
Lesson viewer (/learn/[slug]/[...path]) - Lesson content rendered from Markdown to HTML - Breadcrumb navigation (course → module → lesson) - Previous / Next buttons for sequential reading - Read-only — learners cannot edit content



Staged publishing lets you build a full course in advance and release content incrementally — revealing each week or module only when you are ready for learners to see it.
How it works:
Hidden folders are excluded from the _quarto.yml sidebar automatically. When you commit and push, Quarto renders only the visible content, so hidden weeks do not appear in the GitHub Pages site at all.
Hiding a folder: 1. Open the course in the editor 2. Hover over a week or module folder in the file tree 3. Click the Eye icon that appears — the folder dims and its files are removed from the sidebar 4. Commit and push to apply the change to the live site
Showing a folder: 1. Hover over the dimmed folder 2. Click the Eye-off icon — the folder is restored to the sidebar 3. Commit and push
The _quarto.yml file is updated automatically each time you toggle visibility. You can open it to confirm which sections are included.

SCORM note: If any content is hidden, the SCORM download button in the Git panel is replaced by an amber warning. SCORM packages are designed to deliver a complete course to an LMS — hidden content would leave learners with an incomplete experience. Unhide all folders before downloading a SCORM package.




Click the globe icon again in the editor toolbar to unpublish. The course immediately disappears from the public catalog. The URL returns a 404 until you republish.
Unpublishing does not delete any content — all your files remain intact.

Note: If you have submitted your course for community review, unpublishing does not withdraw the submission. Contact support if you need to withdraw a submitted course.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
AI Forge is the AI copilot built into the editor. It helps you generate, improve, and review course content without leaving the editor.


AI Forge is a set of purpose-built AI workflows and a free-form chat assistant, all powered by Claude (Anthropic). Each workflow is designed around a specific authoring task — generating an outline, drafting a lesson, building an assessment — and produces output formatted for Quarto Markdown.
Open AI Forge by clicking the Forge tab in the right panel.



Every AI Forge action consumes credits from your monthly allowance.



Plan
Credits / Month




Starter
50 (6-month trial, then 0)


Creator
500


Pro
2,000


Enterprise
100,000



Credits are deducted when you click Generate or send a chat message. If generation fails (e.g. due to a network error), the credit is still counted — the AI call was made.
Your remaining credits are shown in the dashboard stats panel and in Settings. Credits reset on the 1st of each month.

Starter trial: New accounts on the Starter plan receive 50 free credits for the first 6 months. After the trial period, the Starter plan remains free forever but AI credits are set to 0. Upgrade to Creator or Pro to continue using AI Forge.






What it does: Generates a complete _quarto.yml course structure plus a brief description of each module and lesson.
When to use it: At the start of a new course, before you’ve written any content. Use it to rapidly scaffold a logical, pedagogically sound structure.
How to use it: 1. Open _quarto.yml in the editor (so the result can be copied in easily) 2. In the Forge tab, select Generate Outline 3. The workflow reads your course title and description automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Review the output and copy it into _quarto.yml, or use Insert to replace the current file content
Output: A YAML Quarto book configuration with module/lesson hierarchy, plus short lesson descriptions.
Tips: - Write a detailed course description before generating — more context produces a better outline - The outline is a starting point; edit the module and lesson names to match your specific content - After editing _quarto.yml, create the corresponding .qmd files in the file tree




What it does: Writes a full lesson in Quarto Markdown, including YAML frontmatter, section headings, practical examples, callout blocks, and a summary.
When to use it: When you need a first draft of a lesson quickly. The draft will need editing but gives you a solid structure to build on.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to draft in the editor 2. In the Forge tab, select Draft Lesson 3. The workflow reads your course title, the current lesson title (from the file’s frontmatter), the _quarto.yml outline, and adjacent lessons for context 4. Click Generate 5. Review the output and click Insert to replace the current file content, or copy manually
Output: A complete .qmd lesson — 800 to 1,500 words, structured with headings, practical examples, and callouts.
Tips: - The more complete your _quarto.yml is, the better the draft — it uses the full outline as context - Draft lessons in order; each draft reads adjacent lesson content for continuity - Always review and edit the draft — AI output requires a human pass for accuracy and voice




What it does: Converts the content of a lesson file into a Reveal.js slide deck in Quarto format (.qmd with format: revealjs).
When to use it: When you need a presentation version of a lesson — for live delivery, recording, or supplementary material.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to convert 2. In the Forge tab, select Generate Slides 3. The workflow reads the current file content automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Create a new file for the slides (e.g. modules/01-introduction/01-slides.qmd) and paste or insert the output
Output: A complete Reveal.js .qmd presentation with: - Title slide, overview slide, content slides, summary slide - Speaker notes in ::: {.notes} blocks - Maximum 6 content lines per slide - Incremental reveals where appropriate
Tips: - Run the Lesson Drafter first, then Slide Generator — you get both a lesson and slides from one workflow - Slide decks should be stored as separate files, not as replacements for lesson files - Speaker notes are a good place to add context that doesn’t fit on the slide




What it does: Creates a quiz with multiple choice questions, short answer questions, and practical exercises based on a lesson’s content.
When to use it: After finishing a lesson, to create a formative or summative assessment.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to assess 2. In the Forge tab, select Build Assessment 3. The workflow reads the current file content automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Create a new file (e.g. modules/01-introduction/assessment.qmd) and paste or insert the output
Output: A .qmd assessment with: - 5–8 questions - Mixed question types (multiple choice, short answer, practical scenario) - Questions ordered from basic recall to applied understanding - Answer keys in collapsible callout blocks
Tips: - Review all answers carefully — AI-generated answer keys can contain errors - Remove or rewrite questions that are ambiguous or too easy - The assessment file should be added to _quarto.yml if you want it visible to learners




What it does: Reviews a lesson against five dimensions and provides specific, actionable feedback.
Review dimensions: 1. Learning Design — Are objectives clear? Does content build progressively? 2. Clarity & Readability — Is the writing clear? Is jargon explained? 3. Accessibility — Are images described? Are headings structured? 4. Completeness — Are all outline topics covered? Are there gaps? 5. Technical Accuracy — Are code examples correct? Are claims accurate?
When to use it: After finishing a first draft of a lesson, before publishing.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson you want reviewed 2. In the Forge tab, select Review Content 3. Click Generate 4. Read the review in the output area — each finding is labelled with severity (🔴 Critical / 🟡 Suggestion / 🟢 Praise) and dimension
Output: A structured review with a score out of 5 for each dimension, individual findings with severity and detail, and a top-3 priority improvements list.
Tips: - Treat 🔴 Critical findings as must-fix before publishing - Run the reviewer again after making revisions — scores improve iteratively - The reviewer works best on longer, more complete lessons




What it does: Takes raw, unstructured content — slide notes, a PDF transcript, rough notes, a blog post — and restructures it into a polished Quarto Markdown lesson.
When to use it: When you have existing material you want to convert into a proper lesson without starting from scratch.
How to use it: 1. In the Forge tab, click the Import tab 2. Paste your raw content into the text area 3. Enter a lesson title 4. Click Structure with AI 5. Review the output. Click Insert to replace the current file, or Create as New File to save it as a new lesson
What it preserves: All factual content, examples, domain terminology, and code snippets from the original.
What it improves: Structure (logical sections), Markdown formatting, callout blocks for key points, a Summary section.
Tips: - Works well with: slide exports, meeting notes, existing blog posts, lecture transcripts, Word documents (paste the plain text) - The longer and richer the source material, the better the output - Always review code blocks in the output — they may need language tags or corrections




What it does: A free-form conversational assistant with full awareness of your course context. Ask it anything about your course, request specific edits, ask for examples, or have it write a section in a particular style.
When to use it: For anything that doesn’t fit the structured workflows — brainstorming, getting unstuck, asking “how should I explain X to a beginner?”, requesting a specific paragraph, or iterating on a draft.
How to use it: 1. In the Forge tab, click the Chat tab 2. Type your message and press Enter (or click Send) 3. The assistant responds in the chat. Each response has Copy and Insert buttons 4. Continue the conversation — the assistant remembers the full message history for the session 5. Click Clear to start a fresh conversation
What the assistant knows: - Your course title and description - The first 3,000 characters of the file currently open in the editor
Tips: - If asking for Markdown content, say “in Quarto Markdown” — it will use the correct callout syntax - For long edits, use Insert to push content directly into the editor, then tidy up - The chat is session-based; it resets when you reload the page or switch courses - Each message sent costs 1 credit





Write a good course description before generating — it’s passed as context to every workflow
Keep _quarto.yml up to date — the outline is used by the Lesson Drafter and Reviewer
Use workflows in sequence — Outline → Lesson Draft → Slide Generator → Assessment Builder → Content Reviewer mirrors the natural authoring flow
Edit every output — AI Forge produces a solid first draft; a human review pass is always needed for accuracy, voice, and nuance
One lesson at a time — workflows operate on the currently open file; keep the relevant lesson open before clicking Generate

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
The editor at /courses/[courseId]/editor is where you spend most of your time in CourseFoundry. It has three main areas: the file tree on the left, the Monaco editor in the centre, and the right panel with four tabs.


┌──────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│              │                             │                   │
│  File Tree   │     Monaco Editor           │  Right Panel      │
│              │                             │  ┌─────────────┐  │
│  _quarto.yml │  # Lesson Title             │  │ Preview     │  │
│  index.qmd   │                             │  │ Forge       │  │
│  modules/    │  Write your content here    │  │ Media       │  │
│    01-mod/   │  using Quarto Markdown.     │  │ Git         │  │
│      01.qmd  │                             │  └─────────────┘  │
│              │                             │                   │
└──────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘
The file tree and right panel can each be collapsed with the toggle buttons in the toolbar to give you more writing space.



The toolbar at the top of the editor contains:



Button
Action




Course title (left)
Returns to the dashboard


Globe / GlobeLock icon
Publish or unpublish the course


Panel left toggle
Show / hide the file tree


Panel right toggle
Show / hide the right panel






The file tree shows all files in your course. Click any file to open it in the editor.
Creating a file Click the + button at the top of the file tree. Enter a file path, including the folder structure if needed (e.g. modules/04-advanced/01-lesson.qmd). The file is created immediately and opened in the editor.

Tip: New lesson files are picked up automatically the next time you toggle a folder’s visibility. If you want to add a file to the published sidebar immediately without changing visibility, open _quarto.yml and add it under website.sidebar.contents.

Renaming a file Hover over a file in the tree and click the rename icon. Enter the new name and press Enter.
Deleting a file Hover over a file and click the delete icon. Confirm deletion in the prompt. File deletion is permanent.
Hiding a folder (Staged Publishing) Hover over any folder in the file tree to reveal action icons. title: Welcome
text:
CourseFoundry is a Markdown-native course authoring platform with a built-in AI assistant (AI Forge). It is designed for people who know their subject deeply and want a professional, structured way to turn that knowledge into a shareable course — without fighting a drag-and-drop editor or paying for bloated enterprise software.
You write in plain Markdown (specifically Quarto Markdown), your files are structured like a real project, and AI Forge handles the heavy lifting: generating outlines, drafting lessons, building slide decks, creating assessments, and reviewing your content.



CourseFoundry is built for three main types of course creator:








Persona
Description
Recommended Plan




Technical Trainer
Freelancer, consultant, or subject matter expert creating professional development or software training
Creator


Lecturer / Academic
University or college educator building structured learning materials
Creator or Pro


L&D Team
Corporate learning and development team running onboarding, compliance, or upskilling programmes
Pro or Enterprise



If you’ve ever felt that consumer platforms like Teachable were built for influencers rather than educators, or that institutional tools like Moodle were too complex for individual use, CourseFoundry sits in the space between.



Before diving in, it helps to understand a few terms used throughout this documentation.
Quarto Markdown (.qmd) CourseFoundry courses are written in Quarto Markdown — a plain-text format that extends standard Markdown with academic and technical features like callout blocks, cross-references, and presentation output. Files use the .qmd extension but are otherwise identical to .md files in most respects. You do not need to install Quarto to use CourseFoundry — the platform handles rendering.
Course A course is a container for your content. It has a title, description, status (draft or published), and a collection of files that make up the lessons, structure, and supporting material.
Course Files Every piece of content inside a course is stored as a file — lessons, the course structure (_quarto.yml), and any supporting documents. Files are organised into modules (folders) within the course. All files are stored securely and privately until you publish.
_quarto.yml This is the course’s configuration and navigation file. It defines the course type (website), a docked collapsible sidebar with nested week/module sections, and settings such as page navigation, reader mode, and search. When you use a template, this file is generated for you. CourseFoundry automatically regenerates the sidebar whenever you toggle a folder’s visibility (see Staged Publishing). title: Getting Started
text:
Go to coursefoundry.com and click Sign Up. You can sign up with:

Email and password — enter your email and choose a password
GitHub — authorises via GitHub OAuth (recommended if you plan to use GitHub integration)
Google — authorises via Google OAuth

After signing up, you will be redirected to your dashboard.

Beta access: During the beta period, accounts must be approved before accessing the authoring tools. If you see a waiting screen after signing up, your account is pending beta activation.




The dashboard at /dashboard is your home base. From here you can:

See all your courses in a card grid, sorted by most recently edited
Create a new course with the New Course button
Duplicate or delete existing courses
View your AI credit usage for the current month
Access Settings for billing and GitHub connection

Each course card shows: - Status badge — Draft (grey) or Published (green) - Community badges — Official, In Community, Pending Review, or Rejected (if submitted for the community catalog) - Last edited date - View button (published courses only) — opens the public learner page - Duplicate icon — creates a copy of the course - Delete icon — opens a confirmation modal before deleting




Click New Course on the dashboard
Step 1 — Choose a template. Select Academic Course if you’re building a structured multi-module course, or Technical Tutorial for a step-by-step guide. For maximum control, choose Blank.
Step 2 — Customise. Set your target audience, estimated duration, number of modules/lessons, and any optional sections (assessments, prerequisites, etc.).
Step 3 — Name it. Enter a course title and optional description. Click Create Course.
The editor opens with a scaffolded file structure. Your _quarto.yml and lesson files are ready to edit.
Click on any lesson file in the file tree. Start writing.
Use AI Forge → Lesson Drafter to generate a first draft of the selected lesson.
When you’re ready, click the globe icon in the toolbar to publish.

text:
The editor at /courses/[courseId]/editor is where you spend most of your time in CourseFoundry. It has three main areas: the file tree on the left, the Monaco editor in the centre, and the right panel with four tabs.


┌──────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬───────────────────┐
│              │                             │                   │
│  File Tree   │     Monaco Editor           │  Right Panel      │
│              │                             │  ┌─────────────┐  │
│  _quarto.yml │  # Lesson Title             │  │ Preview     │  │
│  index.qmd   │                             │  │ Forge       │  │
│  modules/    │  Write your content here    │  │ Media       │  │
│    01-mod/   │  using Quarto Markdown.     │  │ Git         │  │
│      01.qmd  │                             │  └─────────────┘  │
│              │                             │                   │
└──────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴───────────────────┘
The file tree and right panel can each be collapsed with the toggle buttons in the toolbar to give you more writing space.



The toolbar at the top of the editor contains:



Button
Action




Course title (left)
Returns to the dashboard


Globe / GlobeLock icon
Publish or unpublish the course


Panel left toggle
Show / hide the file tree


Panel right toggle
Show / hide the right panel






The file tree shows all files in your course. Click any file to open it in the editor.
Creating a file Click the + button at the top of the file tree. Enter a file path, including the folder structure if needed (e.g. modules/04-advanced/01-lesson.qmd). The file is created immediately and opened in the editor.

Tip: New lesson files are picked up automatically the next time you toggle a folder’s visibility. If you want to add a file to the published sidebar immediately without changing visibility, open _quarto.yml and add it under website.sidebar.contents.

Renaming a file Hover over a file in the tree and click the rename icon. Enter the new name and press Enter.
Deleting a file Hover over a file and click the delete icon. Confirm deletion in the prompt. File deletion is permanent.
Hiding a folder (Staged Publishing) Hover over any folder in the file tree to reveal action icons. Click the Eye icon to hide that folder — all files inside it are excluded from _quarto.yml when the course is published to GitHub Pages. The folder dims to indicate it is hidden. Click the Eye-off icon to make it visible again. See Staged Publishing for the full workflow.
File order Files appear in the sidebar in the order defined by _quarto.yml. The file tree reflects folder and file name order. Use numeric prefixes (01-, 02-) to control sort order.



All lesson files use the .qmd extension and follow standard Markdown syntax with some Quarto-specific additions.
YAML frontmatter Every .qmd file should start with a YAML frontmatter block:
---
title: "Your Lesson Title"
---
This sets the title shown in navigation and as the page heading.
Headings Use ## for main sections and ### for sub-sections. The frontmatter title acts as the H1, so start your body content at H2.
Code blocks Fenced code blocks with a language tag get syntax highlighting:
```python
def hello():
    print("Hello, world!")
```
Callout blocks Quarto callouts draw attention to important content:
::: {.callout-tip}
## Tip Title
Helpful suggestion here.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
Something worth noting.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
A caution or warning.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Critical information.
:::
Collapsible callouts (useful for answer keys):
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
The correct answer is B, because...
:::
Lists
- Unordered item
- Another item

1. Ordered item
2. Second item

- [ ] Task / checklist item
- [x] Completed item
Tables
| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Value    | Value    | Value    |
Links and images
[Link text](https://example.com)
![Alt text](path/to/image.png)
Bold, italic, inline code
**bold**  *italic*  `inline code`



The editor saves your work automatically after 1.5 seconds of inactivity. A subtle indicator in the toolbar shows the save status. There is no manual save button — just write, and your content is preserved.

Note: Autosave writes to the CourseFoundry database. This is separate from GitHub. To save a versioned snapshot to GitHub, use the Git panel (see GitHub Integration).




Click the Preview tab in the right panel to see a rendered version of the file currently open in the editor. The preview updates as you type (with a short debounce delay).
Quarto-specific features rendered in preview: - Callout blocks (.callout-tip, .callout-note, .callout-warning, .callout-important) - Standard Markdown (headings, lists, tables, code blocks, bold, italic)

Note: The preview is a live approximation. The final published output may differ slightly in styling. Full Quarto rendering (cross-references, bibliographies, etc.) is not processed server-side in this version.







Tab
Description




Preview
Live Markdown rendering of the current file


Forge
AI Forge assistant — workflows and chat


Media
Upload images and create placeholder images


Git
GitHub commit, history, and restore






Click the Media tab in the right panel to manage visual assets for your course.
Images tab
Upload image files (PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG, WebP) directly from your computer. Uploaded images are stored in Supabase Storage and served via a CDN. Click any uploaded image to insert a Markdown image tag at your cursor position:
![Image description](https://cdn.../your-image.png)
Placeholders tab
Placeholder images let you mark where a real image will go while you focus on writing content. They are generated as styled SVG files with descriptive text baked in, so your course structure is complete even before photography, diagrams, or screenshots are ready.
To create a placeholder: 1. Select a Content Type: Image, Video, Diagram, Screenshot, or Icon — each uses a distinct colour scheme 2. Select an Aspect Ratio: 16×9, 1×1, 4×3, Portrait, or Banner 3. Enter a Label (the image name shown on the placeholder) and a Description (brief notes about what should go here) 4. Optionally expand Advanced to add an AI prompt (for AI image generation later) or a designer brief 5. Click Create & Insert — the placeholder SVG is uploaded and a Markdown image tag is inserted at your cursor
Existing placeholders are listed below the creation form with a thumbnail. Click the Edit icon on any placeholder to update its label, description, or briefs — the SVG is regenerated in place and the Markdown reference in your files stays valid.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
AI Forge is the AI copilot built into the editor. It helps you generate, improve, and review course content without leaving the editor.


AI Forge is a set of purpose-built AI workflows and a free-form chat assistant, all powered by Claude (Anthropic). Each workflow is designed around a specific authoring task — generating an outline, drafting a lesson, building an assessment — and produces output formatted for Quarto Markdown.
Open AI Forge by clicking the Forge tab in the right panel.



Every AI Forge action consumes credits from your monthly allowance.



Plan
Credits / Month




Starter
50 (6-month trial, then 0)


Creator
500


Pro
2,000


Enterprise
100,000



Credits are deducted when you click Generate or send a chat message. If generation fails (e.g. due to a network error), the credit is still counted — the AI call was made.
Your remaining credits are shown in the dashboard stats panel and in Settings. Credits reset on the 1st of each month.

Starter trial: New accounts on the Starter plan receive 50 free credits for the first 6 months. After the trial period, the Starter plan remains free forever but AI credits are set to 0. Upgrade to Creator or Pro to continue using AI Forge.






What it does: Generates a complete _quarto.yml course structure plus a brief description of each module and lesson.
When to use it: At the start of a new course, before you’ve written any content. Use it to rapidly scaffold a logical, pedagogically sound structure.
How to use it: 1. Open _quarto.yml in the editor (so the result can be copied in easily) 2. In the Forge tab, select Generate Outline 3. The workflow reads your course title and description automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Review the output and copy it into _quarto.yml, or use Insert to replace the current file content
Output: A YAML Quarto book configuration with module/lesson hierarchy, plus short lesson descriptions.
Tips: - Write a detailed course description before generating — more context produces a better outline - The outline is a starting point; edit the module and lesson names to match your specific content - After editing _quarto.yml, create the corresponding .qmd files in the file tree




What it does: Writes a full lesson in Quarto Markdown, including YAML frontmatter, section headings, practical examples, callout blocks, and a summary.
When to use it: When you need a first draft of a lesson quickly. The draft will need editing but gives you a solid structure to build on.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to draft in the editor 2. In the Forge tab, select Draft Lesson 3. The workflow reads your course title, the current lesson title (from the file’s frontmatter), the _quarto.yml outline, and adjacent lessons for context 4. Click Generate 5. Review the output and click Insert to replace the current file content, or copy manually
Output: A complete .qmd lesson — 800 to 1,500 words, structured with headings, practical examples, and callouts.
Tips: - The more complete your _quarto.yml is, the better the draft — it uses the full outline as context - Draft lessons in order; each draft reads adjacent lesson content for continuity - Always review and edit the draft — AI output requires a human pass for accuracy and voice




What it does: Converts the content of a lesson file into a Reveal.js slide deck in Quarto format (.qmd with format: revealjs).
When to use it: When you need a presentation version of a lesson — for live delivery, recording, or supplementary material.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to convert 2. In the Forge tab, select Generate Slides 3. The workflow reads the current file content automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Create a new file for the slides (e.g. modules/01-introduction/01-slides.qmd) and paste or insert the output
Output: A complete Reveal.js .qmd presentation with: - Title slide, overview slide, content slides, summary slide - Speaker notes in ::: {.notes} blocks - Maximum 6 content lines per slide - Incremental reveals where appropriate
Tips: - Run the Lesson Drafter first, then Slide Generator — you get both a lesson and slides from one workflow - Slide decks should be stored as separate files, not as replacements for lesson files - Speaker notes are a good place to add context that doesn’t fit on the slide




What it does: Creates a quiz with multiple choice questions, short answer questions, and practical exercises based on a lesson’s content.
When to use it: After finishing a lesson, to create a formative or summative assessment.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson file you want to assess 2. In the Forge tab, select Build Assessment 3. The workflow reads the current file content automatically 4. Click Generate 5. Create a new file (e.g. modules/01-introduction/assessment.qmd) and paste or insert the output
Output: A .qmd assessment with: - 5–8 questions - Mixed question types (multiple choice, short answer, practical scenario) - Questions ordered from basic recall to applied understanding - Answer keys in collapsible callout blocks
Tips: - Review all answers carefully — AI-generated answer keys can contain errors - Remove or rewrite questions that are ambiguous or too easy - The assessment file should be added to _quarto.yml if you want it visible to learners




What it does: Reviews a lesson against five dimensions and provides specific, actionable feedback.
Review dimensions: 1. Learning Design — Are objectives clear? Does content build progressively? 2. Clarity & Readability — Is the writing clear? Is jargon explained? 3. Accessibility — Are images described? Are headings structured? 4. Completeness — Are all outline topics covered? Are there gaps? 5. Technical Accuracy — Are code examples correct? Are claims accurate?
When to use it: After finishing a first draft of a lesson, before publishing.
How to use it: 1. Open the lesson you want reviewed 2. In the Forge tab, select Review Content 3. Click Generate 4. Read the review in the output area — each finding is labelled with severity (🔴 Critical / 🟡 Suggestion / 🟢 Praise) and dimension
Output: A structured review with a score out of 5 for each dimension, individual findings with severity and detail, and a top-3 priority improvements list.
Tips: - Treat 🔴 Critical findings as must-fix before publishing - Run the reviewer again after making revisions — scores improve iteratively - The reviewer works best on longer, more complete lessons




What it does: Takes raw, unstructured content — slide notes, a PDF transcript, rough notes, a blog post — and restructures it into a polished Quarto Markdown lesson.
When to use it: When you have existing material you want to convert into a proper lesson without starting from scratch.
How to use it: 1. In the Forge tab, click the Import tab 2. Paste your raw content into the text area 3. Enter a lesson title 4. Click Structure with AI 5. Review the output. Click Insert to replace the current file, or Create as New File to save it as a new lesson

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
CourseFoundry autosaves your work continuously to its own database. GitHub integration adds an additional layer: versioned snapshots. Every time you commit, a complete copy of your course files is pushed to a private GitHub repository.
This gives you: - Version history — go back to any previous state - Disaster recovery — restore your course if you accidentally delete content - Portability — your content lives in a standard Git repo you own - GitHub Pages publishing — automatically render and publish your course as a website (see below) - Collaboration potential — others can clone, fork, or contribute via GitHub




Go to Settings (link in the sidebar or top nav)
Scroll to the GitHub section
Click Connect GitHub
You’ll be redirected to GitHub to authorise CourseFoundry
After authorising, you’re returned to Settings with your GitHub username shown

You only need to connect once. The connection persists across sessions.




Open a course in the editor
Click the Git tab in the right panel
Write a commit message describing what you changed (e.g. “Add module 2 lessons” or “Fix assessment answers”)
Click Commit to GitHub

On the first commit for a course, CourseFoundry automatically creates a private GitHub repository named coursefoundry-[course-slug] in your GitHub account. Subsequent commits push to the same repository.
A success message shows the commit SHA and a link to view it on GitHub.
The most recent commit SHA (first 7 characters) is also shown at the bottom of the editor’s left sidebar as a clickable link to the commit on GitHub — so you can always see at a glance what version the course is at.



In the Git tab, the History section shows the last 20 commits for the current course. Each entry shows: - Commit message - Date and time - Author - Short commit SHA




In the Git tab, find the commit you want to restore in the history list
Click Restore next to that commit
A preview of the files from that commit is shown
Confirm to overwrite the current course files with the restored version


Warning: Restoring a commit overwrites your current course files. This action cannot be undone within CourseFoundry. If you have unsaved changes you want to keep, commit them first before restoring an older version.




Synced to GitHub: - All course files (_quarto.yml, .qmd files, etc.) - File content and structure as it exists at the time of commit
Not synced: - Course metadata (title, description, status, slug) — stored in CourseFoundry only - AI credits or usage history - Publish status



Once your course has been committed to GitHub at least once, you can enable GitHub Pages to automatically publish your course as a rendered Quarto website.
How it works:

In the editor, open the Git tab
Scroll to the GitHub Pages section
Click Enable GitHub Pages

CourseFoundry will: - Create a separate public GitHub repository (coursefoundry-[slug]-pages) in your account - Set up an Ed25519 deploy key so the workflow can push rendered output - Add a PAGES_DEPLOY_KEY Actions secret to your source repo - Commit a GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/publish.yml) to your source repo
From that moment on, every commit to your source repo triggers the workflow: 1. Quarto renders your course files (quarto render) → produces _output/ HTML output 2. The rendered site is pushed to the gh-pages branch of the output repo 3. GitHub Pages serves it at https://[your-github-username].github.io/coursefoundry-[slug]-pages/
The Pages URL is shown in the Git panel with a Live badge. The site updates automatically — no manual steps needed after enabling.
The rendered site uses a docked collapsible sidebar for navigation, with reader mode and full-text search built in. Only folders and files that are visible (not hidden via the Eye toggle) appear in the sidebar — hidden weeks or modules are excluded from the published output automatically.
To disable: Click Disable Pages in the Git tab. This removes the workflow file and deploy key. The output repository is left intact in your GitHub account (you can delete it manually if you wish).

Note: GitHub Pages requires your Quarto source files to produce valid output. If quarto render fails (e.g. missing _quarto.yml, broken syntax), the Actions run will fail and the site will not update. Check the Actions tab on your source repo to diagnose failures.





Go to Settings → GitHub
Click Disconnect

Disconnecting removes the OAuth connection from CourseFoundry. Your GitHub repositories and their contents are not affected — they remain in your GitHub account.
To reconnect in future, repeat the connection steps.




Branch per cohort or version
Pull request-based content review workflow
Multi-author collaboration via forks

text:
All your courses appear on the dashboard as cards. They are sorted by most recently edited. Courses are private by default (Draft status) until you publish them.



Click the Copy icon on a course card to duplicate it. The duplicate is created with: - A new title: “[Original Title] (Copy)” - All original files copied - Status set to Draft - A new unique slug
Duplication is useful for creating course variants, seasonal updates, or using an existing course as a starting template.



Click the Trash icon on a course card. A confirmation modal appears explaining exactly what will happen before anything is deleted.
Permanently deleted: - The course record and all metadata - All course files and their content
Not affected: - Your GitHub repository (if linked) — the repo remains in your GitHub account; only the link between CourseFoundry and the repo is removed - AI credits already used — these are not refunded
Click Delete Course in the modal to confirm. Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.



The slug is generated from the course title when the course is created. For example, a title of “Introduction to Smart Manufacturing” becomes the slug introduction-to-smart-manufacturing.
The published URL for a course is: coursefoundry.com/learn/[slug]
Slugs cannot be changed after course creation. If you need a different URL, create a new course with the desired title and migrate your content.

title: CourseFoundry Documentation
text:
Symptom: Clicking Generate produces no output, a timeout error, or a generic “AI generation failed” message.
Causes and fixes: - The AI service can take 15–30 seconds for longer workflows (Lesson Drafter in particular). Wait at least 30 seconds before concluding it has failed. - Check your AI credit balance in Settings. If you have 0 credits, generation will be blocked immediately. - If generation consistently fails, the AI service may be temporarily unavailable. Try again in a few minutes. - Very long file content (over 50,000 characters) will be rejected. Split large files into multiple lessons.




Symptom: Creating a course returns a duplicate title error.
Fix: Course slugs must be unique per account. Choose a different title, or append a year or version number (e.g. “Introduction to Python 2026”).




Symptom: Clicking “Commit to GitHub” shows an error.
Causes and fixes: - Your GitHub connection may have expired. Go to Settings, disconnect, and reconnect. - The repository may have been deleted manually on GitHub. CourseFoundry will attempt to recreate it on the next commit. - GitHub’s API may be temporarily unavailable. Check githubstatus.com and retry. - If you recently revoked CourseFoundry’s GitHub access from your GitHub account settings, reconnect from Settings.




Symptom: You published a course but it doesn’t appear in the catalog.
Causes and fixes: - Allow up to 30 seconds after publishing for the catalog to update. Refresh the page. - Confirm the course is showing as Published (green badge) on your dashboard. If it shows Draft, the publish action may not have saved — click the globe icon again. - If the course appears on your dashboard as Published but is missing from the catalog, try unpublishing and republishing.




Symptom: The lesson list on the public course page doesn’t match what you expect.
Fix: The sidebar order on the rendered site is determined by _quarto.yml. CourseFoundry regenerates this file automatically when you show or hide folders, but if you have manually edited _quarto.yml the auto-regeneration will overwrite your changes the next time you toggle visibility. To fine-tune ordering, open _quarto.yml in the editor — just be aware that a visibility toggle will regenerate it. File and folder names with a numeric prefix (e.g. 01-, 02-) sort alphabetically and therefore control the order reliably.




Credits reset automatically on the 1st of each month. You cannot manually reset them. If you need more credits before the reset, upgrade your plan or wait for the monthly reset.




Yes. Open your course in the editor, click the LMS Export tab in the right panel, then click Download SCORM Package. The package can be uploaded to any SCORM-compliant LMS (Moodle, Blackboard, Brightspace, etc.).

Note: All course content must be visible (not hidden) before downloading a SCORM package. If any folders are hidden via the Eye toggle, an amber warning appears and the download button is replaced with a prompt to unhide all content first.

PDF export is planned for a future release. Your source files are standard Quarto Markdown — if you have GitHub integration enabled, you can clone your repository and run quarto render locally to produce any output format Quarto supports.




Use the Eye toggle in the file tree. Hover over a week or module folder and click the Eye icon to hide it. Hidden folders are excluded from the published sidebar — students cannot navigate to them even if they know the URL.
Each week before you want content to go live: 1. Hover the folder in the file tree and click the EyeOff icon to reveal it 2. The sidebar is regenerated automatically 3. Commit and push — GitHub Actions re-renders the site and the new week appears for students




Yes. All courses are private by default (Draft status). Only you can see your draft courses — not other CourseFoundry users, not the public. Your content is only made public if you explicitly click the Publish button.
Once published, the course is publicly accessible without login. Unpublishing immediately reverts the course to private.




Team collaboration is planned for the Enterprise plan (Phase 17). Currently, each course belongs to one account. As a workaround, you can share a GitHub repository with a collaborator who can make changes outside CourseFoundry and you can sync them via a commit.




Account deletion is currently handled by contacting support. Send a request to support@coursefoundry.com and your account, courses, and data will be deleted within 30 days in accordance with our Privacy Policy.





This document — covers all current features
Support email: support@coursefoundry.com
Feature requests and bug reports: github.com/johnfjennings/coursefoundry/issues (public issue tracker, coming soon)


CourseFoundry is actively developed. Features marked “coming soon” or “planned” are subject to change. This document is updated with each major release.
